note: The venue catalogue. A VENUE is a name with one or more named LAYOUTS under it, because a room reconfigures and each configuration is a different rig. The layout file is the rig; the venue is who owns it and what they call that configuration. This belongs on the hub beside the scores eventually; it is here so the shape gets settled in one place first. A venue may carry more than one layout because a room reconfigures; KeyCode Arena carries both its own rig and the smaller stage rig, and they are different rigs under one name.

shape.name: what people search for
shape.example: true when the venue itself is invented
shape.access: public | locked -- a venue owns its rig and says who may target it
shape.locked_because: what the person is actually missing, in plain words
shape.logo: a file under portal/logos/. Missing is fine: the page draws a monogram.
shape.layouts: [{name, file, placeholder}] -- file is a *.layout.json in readers/lights/
shape.default: which of those layouts is live unless someone says otherwise

venues.name: Desk Rig
venues.note: The default development rig: four PAR7s in a line with a moving head in the centre.

venues.name: KeyCode Stage
venues.note: Our own event, and the only venue here anyone may design for and play. Two rigs under one name because the room reconfigures: the basic bar for a quiet night, the main stage for a full one.
venues.logo_note: Drop the supplied KeyCode logo at portal/logos/ven_keycode.svg (or .png) and it replaces the drawn monogram with no code change.
venues.rig_placeholder_note: We have not been given KeyCode's fixture list. The rig below is a stand-in so the demo runs; it is NOT what is hanging at KeyCode, and it is marked as such wherever it appears. Replace it when the real list arrives.

venues.name: KeyCode Arena
venues.note: The big room. Same event as KeyCode Stage, a rig with about six times as much on it -- a wash bar upstage, beams on the mid truss, zooming washes out front, audience blinders with a strobe outboard of each end, lasers, and a pixel strip framing each side.
venues.rig_placeholder_note: A designed rig, not a measured one. Every device type on it except the laser was read out of a real GDTF file in this repo, so the channel counts and beam angles are the manufacturers' own -- but the plot, the trim heights and the addresses are ours, not KeyCode's. Replace it when the real list arrives.

venues.name: OMNIA
venues.locked_because: This venue has not granted your account access to its rig. Access is granted by the venue to named designers; nothing in this build can request it.
venues.note: A real nightclub, here to show what a venue-controlled rig looks like. We have no relationship with it and no access to its rig.
venues.rig_note: We do not have OMNIA's fixture list. The rig shown is a stand-in so the catalogue renders; it is NOT what is hanging there.
